text:
## Abstract  
We quantified how frequently carbapenem is mentioned among all publicly available Escherichia coli sequencing runs in the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA). Using the BRC Analytics proxies to ENA, we first obtained the current total number of E. coli runs (taxon ID 562) and then enumerated those whose study titles contain the word “carbapenem.” Two API queries retrieved 551 679 total runs and 9 759 carbapenem-related runs, respectively. The resulting fraction is 1.8 % (9 759 / 551 679). This figure provides a data-driven estimate of how common carbapenem-focused studies are within the extensive corpus of E. coli sequencing data, informing the feasibility of downstream meta-analyses on carbapenem resistance.

## I. Introduction  
Background. Carbapenem antibiotics are last-line treatments against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including Escherichia coli. Surveillance of carbapenem resistance often relies on mining public sequencing data; therefore, understanding how much of the available E. coli sequencing output focuses on carbapenem-related research is essential.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The proportion of E. coli runs in ENA that explicitly reference carbapenem in their study metadata had not been quantified.  
Objective & Hypothesis. We aimed to compute the fraction of E. coli ENA runs whose study titles mention “carbapenem.” We hypothesised that such runs constitute a small minority (<5 %) of the total E. coli dataset.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. A descriptive, cross-sectional analysis of ENA run metadata was performed via the BRC Analytics ENA API, chosen for its ability to return total counts and keyword-filtered counts programmatically.  
Materials.  
• ENA via BRC Analytics (`brc_ena_runs`, `brc_ena_search`).  
Procedures.  
1. Total E. coli runs  
   • Tool: `brc_ena_runs`  
   • Arguments: `taxonomy_id="562"`, `limit=1`, `offset=0`  
2. Carbapenem-related E. coli runs  
   • Tool: `brc_ena_search`  
   • Arguments: `taxonomy_id="562"`, `title_contains="carbapenem"`, `limit=1`  
Statistical Analysis.  
- `brc_ena_runs` returns `total_in_ena` = 551 679 (denominator).  
- `brc_ena_search` returns `total_matching` = 9 759 (numerator).  
- Fraction = 9 759 / 551 679 = 0.01768; percentage = 1.8 % (rounded to one decimal).

## III. Results  
Data Presentation.  

Table 1. Counts of E. coli ENA runs and those mentioning “carbapenem.”

| Category | Runs (n) | Percentage of total |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| All E. coli runs in ENA | 551 679 | 100 % |
| Runs with “carbapenem” in study title | 9 759 | 1.8 % |

Findings. Out of 551 679 E. coli runs in ENA, 9 759 include the term “carbapenem” in their study titles, representing 1.8 % of the total.

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. Approximately one in fifty-five E. coli sequencing runs in ENA is associated with studies that explicitly mention carbapenem. This supports the hypothesis that carbapenem-focused datasets are a minority (<5 %) within the broader E. coli sequencing landscape.  
Context. The 9 759 carbapenem-tagged runs span multiple studies, exemplified by PRJEB49334, which investigates gut colonisation by carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae.  
Limitations. Keyword filtering on study titles may underestimate true carbapenem relevance if studies omit the term in titles or focus on carbapenem resistance without naming it. Conversely, some matches may not specifically investigate resistance mechanisms. Metadata completeness and spelling variations can affect counts.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. Carbapenem-related E. coli runs comprise ~1.8 % of ENA’s holdings. Researchers planning large-scale resistance studies may thus need to broaden search criteria (e.g., include abstract or sample attributes) or supplement with additional keywords (e.g., “KPC,” “NDM”) to capture more datasets. Future work could refine the query across multiple metadata fields and incorporate resistance gene annotations for a more sensitive estimate.

## References  
[1] BRC Analytics ENA proxy. Total E. coli runs query. https://brc-analytics.org/api/v1/ena/taxonomy/562?limit=1  
[2] ENA Portal API. E. coli runs with “carbapenem” in study title. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/search?query=tax_eq(562)%20AND%20study_title=%22*carbapenem*%22&limit=1  

## Acknowledgments  
We thank the European Nucleotide Archive and BRC Analytics for providing programmatic access to sequencing run metadata.
